claims.text: Resistance to simultaneous wear and corrosion in high-entropy alloys is governed by formation and rapid self-healing of a dense, adherent passive oxide film.
Surface enrichment of high-oxygen-affinity elements such as Cr or Al produces the protective passive film.
The passive film acts as a chemical barrier against corrosive species.
The passive film is mechanically robust and minimizes wear damage.
The proposed initial material is a homogeneous, single-phase HEA without a pre-existing protective oxide.
High-temperature processing promotes surface segregation of Cr or Al.
High-temperature processing initiates a thin, continuous oxide layer before service.
Oxidation behavior at elevated temperature depends on oxygen availability.
Ion penetration is reduced by the continuous passive film, thereby reducing corrosion.
Material removal under wear is reduced by the continuous passive film.
After abrasion, enrichment of the underlying matrix enables rapid reformation of the protective layer.
The high-temperature-processed HEA will have a lower corrosion current density than the lower-temperature baseline during simultaneous wear and corrosion.
The high-temperature-processed HEA will have higher passive-film resistance than the baseline.
The high-temperature-processed HEA will have lower wear depth than the baseline.
The high-temperature-processed HEA will have a lower coefficient of friction than the baseline.
A non-uniformly enriched baseline lacking a well-formed oxide film will undergo more direct metal-solution attack and higher wear.
The prediction may fail under oxygen-deficient conditions because the film cannot adequately form or reform.
The prediction may fail at temperatures high enough to make the oxide scale unstable or cause spallation.
Identically composed specimens receiving high- and low-temperature processing can provide a controlled comparison under the same NaCl tribocorrosion conditions.
Absence of statistically significant electrochemical and wear improvements, or failure of the oxide to reform after damage, would falsify the hypothesis.
